questions.question: Which organelle is the site of aerobic respiration in eukaryotic cells?

points.text: Mitochondria

questions.question: A student observes a cell under a microscope. It has a cell wall, chloroplasts, and a large permanent vacuole. What type of cell is it?

points.text: Plant cell
points.guidance: Cell wall + chloroplasts + large vacuole = plant cell

questions.question: State the function of the cell membrane.

points.text: Controls movement of substances in and out of the cell
Separates cell contents from external environment

markScheme.exemplarAnswer: Controls movement of substances in and out of the cell. Partially permeable.
commonErrors: Saying 'controls what enters the cell' without mentioning exit

questions.question: Describe the difference between rough and smooth endoplasmic reticulum.

points.text: Rough ER has ribosomes on its surface
Smooth ER does not have ribosomes
Rough ER involved in protein synthesis / transport; Smooth ER involved in lipid/steroid synthesis
points.guidance: Need function difference for full marks

markScheme.exemplarAnswer: Rough ER has ribosomes on its surface and is involved in protein synthesis and transport. Smooth ER lacks ribosomes and is involved in lipid and steroid synthesis.

questions.question: A cell image is 45 mm wide. The actual cell is 30 μm wide. Calculate the magnification. Give your answer as a whole number.

points.text: Converts units correctly: 45 mm = 45,000 μm OR 30 μm = 0.03 mm

questions.question: Explain how the structure of a palisade mesophyll cell is adapted for its function in photosynthesis.

points.text: Many chloroplasts / contains chlorophyll to absorb light
points.guidance: 1 mark for chloroplasts, 1 for chlorophyll/light absorption

points.text: Tall/columnar shape - packed together to maximise light absorption
points.guidance: Accept: large surface area for light

points.text: Thin cell walls - short diffusion distance for CO₂
Large vacuole - pushes chloroplasts to edge near light
Located at top of leaf - first to receive light

markScheme.exemplarAnswer: Palisade cells are adapted for photosynthesis: they contain many chloroplasts with chlorophyll to absorb light energy. Their tall, columnar shape allows them to be packed tightly, maximising light absorption. Thin cell walls provide a short diffusion path for carbon dioxide. A large central vacuole pushes chloroplasts to the edge of the cell, closer to the light source. They are located at the top of the leaf, so they receive light first.
commonErrors: Listing features without linking to function

questions.question: Name the organelle that modifies and packages proteins for secretion.

points.text: Golgi apparatus / Golgi body

questions.question: A student wants to observe onion epidermal cells using a light microscope. Describe how they should prepare a slide and calculate the actual size of a cell if it appears 12 mm wide at ×400 magnification.

points.text: Peel thin layer of onion epidermis
Place on slide, add drop of iodine solution (stain)
Lower cover slip at angle to avoid air bubbles
Actual size = Image size / Magnification = 12 mm / 400 = 0.03 mm = 30 μm
points.guidance: Must show working and correct units

markScheme.exemplarAnswer: Peel a thin layer of onion epidermis and place on a microscope slide. Add a drop of iodine solution to stain the nucleus. Lower a cover slip at an angle to avoid air bubbles. Actual size = 12 mm ÷ 400 = 0.03 mm = 30 μm.

questions.question: Prokaryotic cells differ from eukaryotic cells because they:

points.text: Have DNA free in cytoplasm (no nucleus)
points.guidance: Accept: no true nucleus / nucleoid region

questions.question: Why do muscle cells contain many mitochondria?

points.text: Muscle contraction requires large amounts of ATP
Mitochondria are the site of aerobic respiration which produces ATP
points.guidance: Must link mitochondria to ATP production

markScheme.exemplarAnswer: Muscle cells need lots of ATP for contraction. Mitochondria carry out aerobic respiration to produce ATP, so more mitochondria means more ATP can be produced.
commonErrors: Saying mitochondria 'make energy' (energy cannot be created)
